author: ViceTechnicolour
body:
Initial release 10 months ago on Overcast Network CubeMinecraft is a map inspired by Lyzak's PvP map 'BlockBlock'. The structures and such were rebuilt by me, including several elements that the original contains. You are in a toy-like fortress where you have to capture the other wools; which are legos to win. The team sizes are 16v16 and it is made for small servers. This map was built by me with bedrock supplied on the bottom of the map to prevent teamspleefing. 

Download
Images
YAML

Special thanks to alexanderjoe10 for the server from a while ago!

Spawnkit:
- Leather Armor
- Gold Chestplate
- Iron Sword
- Bow, Infinity I
- Golden Pickaxe, Mining Fatigue 4 (?)
- Wooden Axe
- 64 Logs
- 32 Glass
- 1 health potion
- 12 Apple
- Arrow

(Yes, this is heavily inspired theme-wise from another PvP map.)

replies.author: ViceTechnicolour
replies.body:
Hey,

I understand what you're trying to say. There should be a divide between the two servers however whether this is leaning toward CTW or the map design itself, CTW is a variant of CTF and has been a popular gamemode for a while on several different servers. Not only this, but CTW has been done on several other servers before Overcast took the gamemode and "promoted", maybe even changed it, into what it is today known through the Minecraft community.

It's perfectly fine to have a gamemode that is based on CTW, and actually CTF/CTW is a real life game anyway, just implemented into Minecraft. I though disagree however with saying it's "too easy". It depends on the map design and it's more riskier due to you have to go through your side, go to theirs, and come back without dying. There are several risks you have with that, and it's not just hold down click to mine something and win. It's a lot more advanced and difficult to play.

For the map itself, it is inspired heavily off a map on OCN, but said map is a TDM, not a CTW. All I did was take the theme, and I already credited the initial author in return. Sometimes, inspiration is the best innovation.
